## Context / Problem

`tests/unit/test_opcert_key_copy_leak_tortoise.py::test_signer_test_modules_leave_no_key_copy_in_the_temp_dir` runs `tests/unit/test_opcert_service.py` and `tests/unit/test_opcert_service_integrity.py` in a nested pytest. On the loaded macOS dev host the nested run took 318-360 s, over the 300 s per-test budget in `pyproject.toml`, so the outer test failed with a pytest-timeout (under xdist: a crashed worker). CI passes.

## Root cause (measured; detail in the 2026-11-03 comment)

No sleep, poll interval, lock timeout, or grace period. The idle time is git process startup on this host (about 95% of each git call happens outside git's own runtime; median exec 0.11-0.33 s versus 0.016 s for `/usr/bin/true`), multiplied by the git processes each test starts: about 52 in the test-side `_make_source` (git init, `rebar.init_repo`, `rebar.create_ticket`) and 34-60 inside `jobs.run_job`.

## Approach

Build the authoritative source once per module instead of once per test. Every test in the 2 modules uses it read-only: `jobs.run_job` clones it into a discarded workspace and never pushes (the no-push tests assert exactly that), so one shared instance per module is sound. Replace `_make_source(tmp_path, monkeypatch)` with a module-scoped fixture built under `tmp_path_factory`, with `REBAR_ROOT` set through a `pytest.MonkeyPatch.context()` only while building. The fixture's teardown asserts every ref of the shared source is unchanged, so a test that mutated it fails loudly instead of leaking state. No `cp -R` (a copied `.tickets-tracker` shares the original gitdir). No autouse fixtures; the per-test budget is not raised.

Cutting the git processes inside `jobs.run_job` is production code and is split into a separate follow-up bug (linked `discovered_from`).

## Scope

- `tests/unit/test_opcert_service.py`: module-scoped `authority` fixture replaces per-test `_make_source`.
- `tests/unit/test_opcert_service_integrity.py`: same.
- `tests/unit/test_opcert_key_copy_leak_tortoise.py`: new test that runs nested `pytest --setup-plan` (no test bodies execute) on each module, through `_nested_pytest.run_nested_pytest` with `_subprocess_env.subprocess_env`, and asserts the authoritative source is set up once at module scope.

## Testing

- New `--setup-plan` test fails before the change (no module-scoped source) and passes after.
- Existing tests in both modules pass unchanged in their assertions, including the no-push byte-identity checks.
- Edge: the fixture teardown ref-snapshot check fails if any test writes to the shared source.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The blocking call behind the ~28 s per-test time is identified and recorded on this ticket (git process startup cost times per-test git process count; see the 2026-11-03 comment).
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/test_opcert_service.py tests/unit/test_opcert_service_integrity.py` (with `-p no:xdist`) finishes under 300 s on the dev host; the wall time and the load average at the time are recorded on this ticket, before and after.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/test_opcert_key_copy_leak_tortoise.py` passes on the dev host, with the new `--setup-plan` test included.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` exit 0 with the worktree `.venv/bin` first on PATH.
- [ ] A follow-up bug for reducing the git process count inside `jobs.run_job` is filed with the measured numbers and linked `discovered_from` this ticket.
